chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from his brother Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed more than one-third, and his heirs were witnesses, so they approved that for him. He said: 'It is valid.' Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat said: 'And in my view, this is because they accepted it during his lifetime and acknowledged it.'
ai.seo_question: Is a bequest exceeding one-third valid if the heirs agree to it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a bequest exceeding one-third of the estate, contingent upon the heirs' consent. The narrator, Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, provides a crucial jurisprudential nuance, suggesting that the validity stems from the heirs' acceptance and acknowledgment of the bequest while the deceased was still alive, thereby distinguishing it from post-death ratification. This highlights the Shia legal principle that heirs' consent can override the standard one-third limit, provided the conditions of agreement are met.
